title: Hybrid Semantic Memory (lexical preserved)
context: The AURA 2.0 contract Phase 2 asks for vector recall, contradicting a documented lexical-only decision. Human review settled it: semantic recall is added BESIDE lexical retrieval, which is preserved.
decision: Semantic recall at the existing Retriever seam: EmbeddingProvider abstraction (hashing/ollama/remote), one SemanticVector table in the existing SQLite database, Reciprocal Rank Fusion with a configurable weight, a provider-declared similarity floor measured at 0.24 for hashing, fail-closed degradation to lexical-only, and a remote-embedding consent gate enforced in the provider.
alternatives: Weighted score fusion instead of RRF
One shared min_similarity constant across providers
rejected_alternatives: Making semantic retrieval a runtime dependency
Letting an embedding failure fail a turn
Choosing a similarity floor by intuition rather than from a sweep
consequences: Memory operates indefinitely in lexical-only mode by default; a model swap is detectable and non-destructive at the cost of an explicit reindex; the hashing provider's n-gram limit is documented and measured; the shipped floor comes from a ten-memory fixture and is labelled a small measurement.
